messages.subject: problem with mixture GLM
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to build a GLM as a mixture of two Gaussians in R and STAN.
here's the code:

# generate data
set.seed(1)
N <- 1000
df <- data.frame(x1=runif(N,-1,1), x2=runif(N,-1,1), x3=runif(N,-1,1))
X <- model.matrix(~.,df)          # the model matrix (contains intercept)
betas1 <- runif(4, -1,1)  
betas2 <- runif(4, 2,4)

r.norm.mix <- function(n,p,m1,m2,sigma) {    
  weight <- runif(n)<p
  rnorm(n,mean=ifelse(weight,m1,m2),sd=sigma)
}

y <- r.norm.mix(1000, p=0.8, m1=X%*%betas1, m2=X%*%betas2, sigma=1)
hist(y,30) # visualization


# STAN model

library(rstan)

model_string <-"
data {
  int<lower=1> K; // number of mixture components
  int<lower=1> N; // number of data points
  int<lower=1> M; //the number of columns in the model matrix
  matrix[N,M] X; //the model matrix
  real y[N]; // observations
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta; // mixing proportions
  vector[M] betas1;
  vector[M] betas2;
  real<lower=0> sigma[K]; // sigmas of mixture components
}
model {
  for(m in 1:M) {
    betas1[m] ~ normal(0,100);
    betas2[m] ~ normal(0,100);
  }
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

  for (n in 1:N) {
    increment_log_prob(log_mix(theta,
      normal_log(y[n], X[n,]*betas1, sigma[1]),
      normal_log(y[n], X[n,]*betas2, sigma[2])));
  }
}
"

m <- stan(model_code = model_string, data = list(X=X, M=ncol(X), K=2, y = y, N = nrow(X)))


this model immediately crashes R and I'm out of ideas. Thanks

messages.author: 40bef15e0492270c
messages.subject: Re: problem with mixture GLM
parts:
Hi Chris,

If you read the manual, log_mix is defined for binary mixtures, and hence only takes a single real as input. I'm not sure if that's what is causing the crashes, but it might be related!

Cheers,
David

mixtures, see the manual chapter on mixture modeling. Basic
idea is that lambda is a K-simplex and if lp is a K-vector of
densities for the components, then you want

increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(log(lambda) + lp));

for (n in 1:N) {
